title: Verify opum-workflow content actually re-fetches through ref:main at the next release
summary: Follow-up from OMARK-32, filed rather than left as an open acceptance criterion with no forward pointer. OMARK-32 repointed opum-workflow's marketplace source to an explicit ref: main, and verified the marketplace LISTING half live (claude plugin marketplace update opum correctly refreshed the clone and parsed the new source), but could NOT verify the content-refetch half: claude plugin install opum-workflow@opum reported 'already installed' because the CLI's own update-dedup logic keys off the declared version string, frozen at 0.4.0 by the current release hold, and never attempted a fetch through the new source path at all. Even a forced attempt would have been inconclusive right now: nothing inside opum-workflow's own content (skills/hooks/plugin.json) differs between the pre-migration commit and main's current tip, so a genuine refetch and a skipped one would look identical in installed_plugins.json's gitCommitSha either way. This task exists so the fetch-through-ref:main path's first REAL exercise -- the next actual opum-workflow version bump, i.e. the eventual stacked release currently held until OMARK-21's observation window closes -- gets checked rather than assumed to have worked.

acceptanceCriteria.text: When the next opum-workflow version bump ships (plugin.json's version field changes and that change is promoted to main), run claude plugin marketplace update opum in a live session, then claude plugin install opum-workflow@opum, and confirm installed_plugins.json's opum-workflow@opum entry actually advances: gitCommitSha becomes a commit reachable from main's new tip, version matches the new plugin.json, lastUpdated moves.

If it does NOT advance as expected, do not silently work around it -- record what actually happened (stuck on old version, wrong content, error) as the first real finding about this migration's design, since nothing before this point could have caught it.
